newsitem.title: USA: Brinker to buy back up $150 mln of shares.
newsitem.headline: Brinker to buy back up $150 mln of shares.

text.p: Brinker International Inc said Tuesday it wil repurchase up to $150 million of its shares in an open market transaction and will realign management that supports its casual dining concepts.

Ron McDougall, president and chief executive officer, said the stock repurchase is designed to return value ot the company's shareholders while strengthening the company's balance sheet and preserving its operating flexibility.

Brinker disclosed the plans as it reported that its revenues for its fiscal 1997 second quarter ended December 25 rose 7.3 percent to $310.9 million, while net income, excluding restructuring items recorded in fiscal 1996 dropped 9.9 percent to $11.6 million to $12.9 million.

"While we are pleased to see continuing positive sales, we are disappointed that the extraordinary margin pressure we experienced in the second quarter -- and especially in the month of December -- reduced earnings so sharply," he said.
He said the lower margins were due to higher commodity prices and labor costs.
Because of this, he said, the company has launched a review of all cost factors affecting its business and is realigning its management structure, among other actions.
